chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Samaan, who said:

I asked him about food (qitrah), dates, and raisins, and he said: 'It is not permissible to exchange two of one type for one of another, unless you change the type to a different type. So if you change the type, there is no objection to exchanging two for one, or more.'

key_terms.الطَّعَامِ: Qitrah (a specific type of dried food, often referring to a mixture or a specific commodity like dried meat or grain, distinct from dates and raisins)
key_terms.فَضْلٌ: Excess (referring to giving more of one commodity for less of another in exchange)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging different quantities of the same type of food commodity in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the application of *riba al-fadl* (excess) specifically to dried staple foods like dates and raisins, distinguishing between same-type exchanges (which require equality) and different-type exchanges (which allow excess). It reflects the Shia juristic consensus that these items are subject to the six *riba* categories, ensuring commercial fairness by preventing hidden interest in bulk commodity trades. The ruling emphasizes that the prohibition applies strictly when the commodity type remains identical, allowing flexibility when converting between distinct varieties.
